question: What is the main focus of health promotion compared to disease prevention?

options.A: Isolating sick patients from healthy community members
options.B: Treating existing diseases with pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: Taking a broad, positive view of overall well-being
options.D: Stopping specific illnesses before they begin

explanation: Health promotion looks at health as a positive resource for daily living rather than just targeting the absence of a specific disease. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T5#BMP117_U1_T5_h1)

question: How does health promotion change the relationship between health workers and patients?

options.A: Midwives take total control over every decision made in the household
options.B: Communities rely completely on government funding for survival
options.C: Medical staff stop treating illnesses to focus only on record keeping
options.D: Patients become active partners instead of passive receivers of care

explanation: By enabling people to take control, health promotion transforms patients into active participants in their own health journey. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T5#BMP117_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the five core action areas of the Ottawa Charter?

options.A: Building healthy public policy across non-health sectors
options.B: Enforcing mandatory hospital admissions for all pregnant women
options.C: Creating supportive environments that make healthy choices easy
options.D: Reorienting health services toward prevention and promotion

explanation: Forced admissions are not part of the Ottawa Charter, which focuses instead on empowerment, supportive environments, and skill-building. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T5#BMP117_U1_T5_h2)

question: A midwife teaches young mothers in the market square how to prepare balanced weaning foods using local crops. Which Ottawa Charter action area does this best represent?
explanation: Teaching individuals practical life skills like food preparation directly supports the development of personal health skills. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T5#BMP117_U1_T5_h2)

question: What do the Social Determinants of Health primarily refer to?

options.A: The non-medical conditions in which people live and grow
options.B: The types of pharmaceutical drugs available in private pharmacies
options.C: The genetic mutations passed down from parents to children
options.D: The specific protocols used by doctors inside the operating room

explanation: These encompass environmental, economic, and social factors outside the clinical setting that influence overall health. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T5#BMP117_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why must a Nigerian midwife understand local social determinants when caring for pregnant women?

options.A: Understanding social factors replaces the need to check blood pressure or urine
options.B: Economic status is the only reliable way to diagnose malaria in pregnancy
options.C: Factors like poverty and literacy directly affect health decisions and access to care
options.D: Midwives are legally required to manage the financial budgets of local households

explanation: Social realities like transport costs, literacy, and gender norms deeply influence whether a woman reaches the clinic safely. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T5#BMP117_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the main benefit of involving local leaders and Village Health Committees in primary health care?

options.A: It completely removes the need for trained midwives in rural areas
options.B: It allows the government to stop spending money on public health
options.C: It builds community ownership and ensures long-term sustainability
options.D: It ensures that traditional practices replace all modern medicine

explanation: Involving the community creates a sense of ownership, making health programs last long after external support ends. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T5#BMP117_U1_T5_h4)

question: A primary health clinic notices low antenatal clinic attendance. What is the best community approach to address this?

options.A: Close the clinic down until community members start coming voluntarily
options.B: Report all pregnant women who miss appointments to local police officers
options.C: Hold a town hall meeting with local leaders and women to discuss barriers
options.D: Print posters in English and place them inside the locked clinic doors

explanation: Engaging the community directly through dialogue helps uncover the real reasons behind low attendance so collaborative solutions can be found. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T5#BMP117_U1_T5_h4)

question: What primary activity defines the midwife's role as a health educator?

options.A: Financially supporting impoverished families out of personal salary funds
options.B: Writing national health policies and passing laws in the legislative assembly
options.C: Managing the administrative budget of the entire local government area
options.D: Translating complex medical advice into simple, relatable information for clients

explanation: A health educator breaks down health concepts so that everyday mothers and families can easily understand and apply them. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T5#BMP117_U1_T5_h5)

question: When a midwife lobbies local authorities to fix bad roads leading to the maternity clinic, what role is she performing?
explanation: Standing up for community needs and pushing leaders for systemic improvements is the core definition of health advocacy. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T5#BMP117_U1_T5_h5)
